checks.detail: The manifest, dist tree, and source hash map contain the same 59 paths with no missing or unlisted file.
All 59 current worktree files and all 59 frozen dist snapshots independently match source_sha256.json.
validate.py main() returned 0 when rerun against a temporary artifact copy, preserving the frozen artifact. Its reported result was Passed with 11 Passed checks.

The inspected HTTP, AppServices, Gate, and PostgreSQL paths enforce verified user context, named capabilities, case scope, bounded types and sizes, digest validation, stable error codes, no-store responses, and minimized upload receipts. Major lifecycle and downstream-source defects remain below.
The byte publication and database commit protocol has uncovered exit paths that retain staging state and the final object, and the validator's cleanup check does not exercise or detect them.

findings.title: A failure before opening the final commit transaction leaves PHI bytes and staging state indefinitely
evidence: dist/crates/aso-web-server/src/adapters/gate.rs:1120-1134 writes the final content-addressed object and cleans up only when write_verified itself fails.

dist/crates/aso-web-server/src/adapters/gate.rs:1136 obtains the final database transaction with begin_document_upload(context).await?; session expiry, pool acquisition failure, or role/context setup failure returns immediately without abandon_document_upload_staging or delete_if_matches.
dist/crates/aso-web-server/src/adapters/gate.rs:606-623 makes cleanup best-effort and silently ignores both staging-abandon and object-delete failures.

dist/migrations/server/2026090620_document_upload_schema.sql:135-138 records an expiry, but the frozen artifact has no sweeper or restart reconciliation that removes expired staging rows and matching final objects.
findings.impact: The blocking atomic-commit-cleanup constraint is not met. A normal expiry or availability failure after object publication can leave a PHI-bearing final object and a staging row with no committed receipt, and a process crash at the same point has the same result.
findings.required_fix: Cover every exit after successful object publication with durable reconciliation. On startup and periodically, reconcile staged rows by command receipt and expiry, deleting only digest-matching uncommitted objects; add a local integration test that forces failure before final transaction acquisition and proves both database staging and final object cleanup or recoverable reconciliation.

findings.title: Uploaded PDF and text sources are reopened as application/octet-stream
evidence: dist/migrations/server/2026090620_document_upload_schema.sql:319-320 derives extensionless keys of the form documents/{practice}/{document}/{sha256}.
dist/crates/aso-web-server/src/adapters/gate.rs:380-390 derives source media type only from .pdf, .png, .jpg, or .jpeg suffixes and otherwise returns application/octet-stream.

dist/crates/aso-web-server/src/adapters/gate.rs:47-53 omits media_type from DocumentSourceGrant, and lines 1250-1259 populate DocumentSource.media_type from the extensionless storage key instead of the authoritative documents.media_type column.
findings.impact: Every document accepted by Web-04 loses its declared PDF/text type at the existing source port once it becomes readable. Downstream processing cannot reliably select the PDF or UTF-8 text path, so the accepted durable object is not usable through the shell-neutral source contract.
findings.required_fix: Return the authoritative media_type in the document source grant and populate DocumentSource.media_type from that typed value. Add an integration assertion that committed PDF and text uploads reopen with application/pdf and text/plain respectively.

findings.title: The validator reports atomic cleanup without testing the claimed state
evidence: validate.py:88-96 marks atomic-rollback-and-cleanup Passed from two receipt labels and then states that no staging residue remains.

dist/scripts/test-web04-document-upload-schema.py:214-218 marks rolled_back_commit_leaves_no_partial_ready_metadata Passed only when stagingCount is 1, so this evidence explicitly retains staging state.
dist/scripts/test-web04-document-upload-service.py checks only for temporary .upload-* files; it does not force a post-write database failure or check for an orphaned final content-addressed object.
The mounted HTTP lifecycle exercises success, retry, conflict, integrity, anonymous, and foreign-tenant paths, but no final-commit setup failure.
findings.impact: The artifact can reach a Passed validation result while the blocking atomic-commit-cleanup condition is unproved and currently false on uncovered paths. This is a false-readiness defect in the review evidence, independent of the product defect in WEB04-CRITIC-001.
findings.required_fix: Replace the label-based check with assertions over database staging rows, committed receipts, temporary files, and final objects after injected failures at each boundary: reserve commit, object publication, final transaction acquisition, final SQL execution, and uncertain commit response.

findings.title: validate.py does not hash the persisted snapshots it claims to validate
evidence: validate.py:39-47 hashes only ROOT/name and checks only existence for ARTIFACT/dist/name.
validate.py:73-75 labels this source-snapshots and says current inputs match persisted snapshots even though snapshot bytes are never compared.
findings.impact: A modified dist snapshot would still pass validate.py as long as the corresponding current worktree file matched source_sha256.json. The present snapshots do match because the critic checked them independently, but the validator does not enforce that property.
findings.required_fix: Hash both ROOT/name and ARTIFACT/dist/name against each expected digest and report current and snapshot mismatches separately.

findings.title: Artifact type metadata disagrees between the manifest and constraints
evidence: constraints.json declares artifact_type content for the same Rust, SQL, and Python artifact.
findings.impact: Schema validation permits the mismatch, but consumers that select checks by artifact type can apply the wrong review profile.
findings.required_fix: Declare the same code artifact type in both metadata files and add a cross-file consistency assertion to validate.py.
